decisions.summary: An unstart followed by a new start resets the task's count of make static runs, and task-unstart takes no WHY
decisions.why: FR-007, which carries the GM's approved improvement 2, refuses a third make static in one task since its last landing. FR-012 requires every escape from that refusal to carry a recorded reason of two words or more. Under D9 a session can run static, static, then task-unstart and task-start, and its next static is the first of a fresh count, though no landing came between. That makes task-unstart an escape from FR-007 with no reason recorded. 'The unstart's row in the log is the record of it' is a record, not a reason, and the GM's approval asked for real enforcement, not instructions. Nothing makes the rule impossible to keep, and nothing in the GM's words implies the carve-out. It should read one of two ways: (a) static_runs_hooks counts the task's runs since its last landing whatever unstarts lie between, which is FR-007's own words; or (b) task-unstart takes WHY= of two words or more, and an unstart that resets the count is recorded in the escape log as FR-012 requires. The rest of D9 stands: a task unstarted and never started again owes no closing order.

decisions.summary: The removal of a withdrawn task's unfilled template stub owes no plan review
decisions.why: The plan-stage gate exists so that a plan's decisions do not reach a tick without an independent verdict. A byte-for-byte template stub holds no decisions, and its removal decides nothing. Requiring a verdict on it asks for a review of nothing, and exempting it does not weaken what the gate is for.

decisions.summary: As worded, the exemption reaches any (removed) block whose own task's box carries ' Withdrawn YYYY-MM-DD: ', in tasks.md or tasks-done.md. It is not bounded to a block that was the template, or to a line written by the command.
decisions.why: One justification is stretched over two unlike things. 'Nothing was decided in it' is true of the template stub (D15a) and false of a filled or reviewed section. The block's own control row shows that a box can be ticked by hand and that this gate is what catches it. Under D15 as worded, a hand-written ' Withdrawn 2026-11-26: x' on a box, with its filled section deleted, passes the tick and the push's plan check with no verdict. D2 and D3 refuse that case only inside make task-withdraw, not at the gate. That is the plan-stage gate's purpose gutted for a case the argument does not reach. It contradicts the GM's 'let's make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement and not just instructions'. In the exemption, in_scope should owe nothing only for a (removed) block whose earlier text is the template stub, by D2's own test (plan::template::TEMPLATE with the id filled in, with or without the performance checklist). A removed block of any other text still owes its verdict, whatever its box says. A red fixture should be pinned beside the existing test: a Withdrawn-form box whose filled block was removed is still answered for.

decisions.why: The tooling speeds no engine, check, gate, landing or builder's loop, and measures no time. So FR-013's ordering applies to it as written.
